fact: Proper protein folding is essential for organelle and cell homeostasis, and cells have evolved elaborate quality control mechanisms to recognize, refold, sequester, or degrade misfolded proteins.
source_span: Proper protein folding is essential for organelle and cell homeostasis . Proteins may fail to achieve or retain their functional conformations due to genetic or environmental insults and cells have evolved elaborate protein quality control ( QC ) mechanisms to combat misfolding . QC systems recognize and refold misfolded proteins and , when not possible , sequester or degrade them to prevent their often deleterious accumulation ( Kevei et al . , 2017 ) .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains why protein quality control is biologically important.

fact: The ubiquitin-proteasome system degrades many misfolded proteins by tagging them with ubiquitin chains that target them for destruction by the 26S proteasome.
source_span: Such degradation frequently occurs via the ubiquitin-proteasome system ( UPS ) , where substrates are modified with ubiquitin leading to their destruction by the 26S proteasome ( Metzger et al . , 2012 ) . Ubiquitin modification requires the action of ubiquitin-activating enzyme ( E1 ) , followed by either sequential or concerted activity of ubiquitin-conjugating enzymes ( E2 ) and substrate-specific ubiquitin ligases ( E3 ) . Multiple rounds of ubiquitination result in polyubiquitin chains , which can serve as targeting signals for recognition and degradation by 26S proteasomes ( Akutsu et al . , 2016; Thrower et al . , 2000 ) .
selection_reasoning: This explains the general mechanism of protein degradation relevant to the study.

fact: Distinct ubiquitin-proteasome system machinery mediates localized quality control of misfolded proteins at different subcellular locations such as the ribosome, endoplasmic reticulum, nucleus, and cytosol.
source_span: Distinct , yet overlapping UPS machinery found at different subcellular locations mediates localized QC of misfolded proteins ( Sontag et al . , 2017 ) . The degradation of misfolded proteins at the ribosome , endoplasmic reticulum ( ER ) , nucleus , inner nuclear envelope , and cytosol is mediated by dedicated UPS machinery ( Boban and Foisner , 2016; Brandman and Hegde , 2016; Comyn et al . , 2014; Gamerdinger , 2016; Jones and Gardner , 2016; Zattas and Hochstrasser , 2015 ) .
selection_reasoning: This contextualizes the study by showing that subcellular QC pathways exist but mitochondrial pathways are less understood.

selection_reasoning: This explains the biological importance of mitochondrial protein quality control.

fact: In mammalian cells, the Parkin and PINK1 ubiquitin-dependent mitophagy pathway removes damaged mitochondria, but in yeast mitophagy primarily adapts to metabolic changes and is not ubiquitin-dependent.
source_span: In mammalian cells , the well-characterized Parkin and PINK1 ubiquitin-dependent mitophagy pathway removes portions of , or entire , damaged mitochondria ( McWilliams and Muqit , 2017; Pickles et al . , 2018 ) . In yeast , however , mitophagy appears to function primarily to adapt to metabolic changes , rather than in protein QC ( Fukuda and Kanki , 2018; Kanki et al . , 2015 ) . Furthermore , there is little evidence indicating that mitophagy is ubiquitin-dependent , in accordance with the absence of obvious yeast orthologues of Parkin or PINK1 ( Belgareh-Touzé et al . , 2017; Tan et al . , 2016 ) .
selection_reasoning: This highlights the difference in mitochondrial quality control between yeast and mammals, justifying the focus on yeast MAD pathways.

fact: Thermal limits for RRV transmission differ from other mosquito-borne diseases, with lower limits constrained by fecundity and survival at all stages and upper limits constrained by fecundity and adult lifespan.

fact: Temperature affects reported human Ross River virus (RRV) cases with a lag of about 8 to 10 weeks due to the time needed for mosquito population growth, virus incubation, and human symptom development and reporting.

This lag between temperature and reported human cases arises from the time it takes for mosquito populations to increase , bite humans and reservoir hosts , acquire RRV , become infectious , and bite subsequent hosts; for pathogens to incubate with vectors; for humans to potentially develop symptoms , seek treatment , and report cases .

fact: Ross River virus transmission by the mosquito Culex annulirostris in inland areas shifts southward as temperatures increase from spring into summer.

fact: A mechanistic unimodal thermal model explains both broad-scale and previously contradictory local-scale patterns of temperature effects on Ross River virus transmission.

fact: Thermal responses of mosquito traits were fit using Bayesian inference with Brière or quadratic functions to capture asymmetrical or symmetrical temperature effects.
source_span: We fit thermal responses of each trait using Bayesian inference with the ‘r2jags’ package ( Plummer , 2003; Su and Yajima , 2009 ) in R ( R Core Team , 2017 ) . Traits with asymmetrical thermal responses were fit as Brière functions: qT ( T–Tmin ) ( Tmax–T ) 1/2 ( Briere et al . , 1999 ) . Traits with symmetrical thermal responses were fit as quadratic functions: -q ( T–Tmin ) ( T–Tmax ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes the key methodological approach to modeling temperature effects on vector traits.

fact: The study used mosquito fecundity and adult survival data from McDonald et al. (1980) to fit thermal response models for mosquito life-history traits.
source_span: The fecundity and adult survival data in McDonald et al . ( 1980 ) were published as time series of one experimental population at each temperature . The resulting data needed to be transformed to fit the corresponding trait thermal responses .
selection_reasoning: Using empirical life-history data to model thermal responses is a key methodological step supporting the study's main findings.

fact: Mosquito survival data were converted from percent surviving over time into lifespan data to fit thermal response models.
source_span: For survival , McDonald et al . reported the percent surviving approximately every other day ( hereafter: ‘semi-daily’ ) . We used these data—along with the number of female adults alive on the first day of oviposition at each temperature—to generate a semi-daily time series estimating the number surviving . To generate the dataset that we used to directly fit the thermal responses , we converted this time series into the number of female individuals who died on each day ( i . e . lifespan data ) .
selection_reasoning: Transforming survival data into lifespan data is a key data processing step enabling accurate thermal response modeling.

fact: Mosquito fecundity data were adjusted by binning over gonotrophic cycle durations and weighting by survival to better reflect daily fecundity in a non-synchronized population.
source_span: Because the population was synchronized , and because mosquitoes lay discrete clutches of eggs separated by several days ( the gonotrophic cycle duration ) , there were many data points when the populations did not produce offspring . These zero-inflated fecundity data are not ideal for fitting thermal responses . Therefore , after digitizing the semi-daily fecundity time series , we binned periods of several days ( the bin size varied by temperature , since the gonotrophic cycle duration varies with temperature ) and took a survival-weighted average within each bin ( so days with more individual mothers contributing to offspring production counted more ) . To generate the dataset that we used to directly fit the thermal responses , we weighted the values within each bin by the mean number of surviving mothers in that bin . This approach allowed us to more accurately reflect daily fecundity averaged over a non-synchronized mosquito population .
selection_reasoning: Adjusting fecundity data to account for mosquito reproductive biology and survival is critical for accurate thermal response modeling, a core methodological claim.

fact: The study used the genus name Aedes for mosquitoes despite a recent taxonomic proposal to elevate some subgenera to genus status, reflecting current consensus.
source_span: In 2000 there was a proposed shift in mosquito taxonomy: several subgenera within the genus Aedes were elevated to genus status ( Wilkerson et al . , 2015 ) . This change affected Aedes vigilax and Aedes camptorhynchus , which were called Ochlerotataus vigilax and Ochlerotatus camptorhynchus for a time by some researchers . More recently , there has been a consensus to return to the previous naming system , so we use Aedes here , although many of the papers we cite use Ochlerotatus instead .
selection_reasoning: Clarifying mosquito taxonomy is important background for understanding the species studied and aligning terminology with current consensus.

fact: In the neurofeedback-reaching (NR) task, monkeys modulated their motor cortical beta power to control a beta cursor and then performed a reaching movement to a peripheral target.
source_span: In the neurofeedback-reaching ( NR ) task monkeys performed neurofeedback immediately followed by an arm reach to a peripheral target ( Figure 1b , c ) . ... Subjects modulated their endogenous neural signals to make the beta cursor hover over the beta target for 450 ms to successfully end the neurofeedback epoch .
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes the key experimental paradigm combining neurofeedback of beta oscillations with motor reaching, central to the study.

fact: The beta neurofeedback cursor reflected endogenous beta oscillatory activity in motor cortex estimated from local field potentials (LFPs) recorded from implanted electrodes.
source_span: The beta neurofeedback cursor was designed to reflect endogenous beta oscillatory events in motor cortex . To calculate its position at each time point ( every 100 ms ) , LFP signals from three channels in the most anterior part of the implanted multi-electrode array were manually selected for each subject .
selection_reasoning: Explains the neural signal basis of the neurofeedback cursor, important for understanding the mechanism of neurofeedback.

fact: Subjects had to hold the beta cursor over a target for 450 ms to complete the neurofeedback epoch and then reach a peripheral target to receive a liquid reward.
source_span: Subjects modulated their endogenous neural signals to make the beta cursor hover over the beta target for 450 ms to successfully end the neurofeedback epoch . ... Once subjects reached the peripheral target and held for 200 ms , they received a liquid reward .
selection_reasoning: Describes the task requirements and reward contingencies, key for interpreting behavioral performance.

fact: If subjects failed to complete the neurofeedback epoch within 60 seconds or failed to hold or reach the peripheral target, no reward was given and the trial ended with an error.
source_span: No reward was given for trials in which the subject did not successfully complete the neurofeedback epoch within 60 s ( neurofeedback timeout error ) , hold in the peripheral reach target for the full 200 ms ( hold errors ) , or in which the subject did not reach the peripheral target within 5 s ( timeout error ) .
selection_reasoning: Specifies the error conditions and task constraints, relevant for understanding task difficulty and performance.

fact: A subject-specific linear transform was used to map normalized beta power estimates to vertical screen positions for the beta cursor.
source_span: Once βest was computed , a subject-specific linear transform was used to map βest to a vertical screen position .
selection_reasoning: Describes the method of converting neural signals into cursor movement, important for understanding the neurofeedback mechanism.

fact: Initial training on the beta neurofeedback task started with lenient beta target requirements that became more stringent as subjects improved.
source_span: Initial training began with more lenient beta neurofeedback requirements ( values to achieve low beta and high beta target were closer to the mean beta cursor value ) . As subjects improved in performance , the beta targets moved further apart until the top and bottom targets had a mean time to target of 5–10 s .
selection_reasoning: Provides insight into the training progression and task difficulty adjustment, relevant for interpreting learning effects.

fact: Monkey G performed a variant of the neurofeedback-reaching task where the beta cursor's horizontal position was controlled by normalized 1–10 Hz power in addition to vertical control by beta power.
source_span: Monkey G performed one task variant of the NR task where the neurofeedback cursor in the x-axis was controlled with normalized 1–10 Hz power in addition to it being controlled in the y-axis with normalized beta power , as described above .
selection_reasoning: Describes an experimental variant testing control of multiple frequency bands, relevant for understanding task complexity and neural control.

fact: Task performance was assessed by comparing actual beta cursor control to a target-shuffled simulation to determine if performance exceeded chance levels.
source_span: For each session ( typically lasting 10–40 min ) , beta cursor position from the session’s online performance was re-run through a target-shuffled task simulation , designed to assess whether the subjects’ performance during the beta neurofeedback epoch of the NR task was resulted merely from chance fluctuations in beta power or was caused by volitional changes in beta power that were specific for the beta target on the screen .
selection_reasoning: Explains the method used to verify that neurofeedback performance was due to volitional control rather than chance, a key validation step.

fact: The study used a simulation of a beta cursor task where success was measured by the number of beta targets acquired within a session.
source_span: In the simulation , after the beta cursor entered the beta target and held for the 450 ms beta target hold time , an average arm-reaching time , the constant reward time , and the constant inter-trial interval time transpired to simulate the natural pacing of the task . At the end of the simulation , a metric of chance performance was the mean number of successful beta targets acquired over the length of the session .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the core behavioral task and performance metric used in the study, which is central to understanding the experimental design and findings.

fact: One hundred simulations were run per session to generate a distribution of rewarded targets per minute, which was used to calculate z-scores for actual performance.
source_span: One hundred simulations were run per session ( each session ~10–40 min ) yielding a distribution of rewarded targets/minute . The mean and standard deviation of the distribution was calculated , and used to z-score the actual number of rewarded trials .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the method used to quantify performance relative to chance, a key analytic approach relevant to the study's conclusions.

fact: Beta oscillatory events were identified by filtering local field potential signals at 25–40 Hz and applying a threshold based on the 60th percentile of amplitude values from rewarded trials.
source_span: The local field potential ( LFP ) signal from one of the electrodes used in the neurofeedback task was selected , and filtered at 25–40 Hz with a fifth order Butterworth filter . The amplitude of the filtered signal was estimated with the Hilbert transform . Each day , a distribution of amplitude values was computed by aggregating all rewarded trials from that day . A threshold was set at the 60th percentile of the resultant distribution .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the key method for detecting beta oscillations, which is central to the study's investigation of beta activity and its behavioral relevance.

fact: Beta oscillatory events shorter than 125 ms were excluded to ensure that only sustained oscillations lasting at least 3–4 cycles were analyzed.
source_span: Then , the length of each block of uninterrupted '1s' was computed , and if the block was longer than 125 ms ( so the oscillatory episode lasted at least 3–4 cycles as described in Murthy and Fetz ( 1996a ) ; Sherman et al . , 2016 ) , the block remained as is . If the block was less than 125 ms , all points in the block were changed back to '0s' .
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies the criteria for defining meaningful beta oscillations, which is important for interpreting the study's findings about beta activity.

fact: A threshold of 3.5 cm/sec hand speed was used to distinguish slow from fast movement timepoints in the analysis.
source_span: Throughout the study slow and fast timepoints are distinguished . A threshold of 3 . 5 cm/sec applied to hand speed was used to separate slow from fast . This threshold was chosen because using it yielded the best discrete classifier performance separating slow spiking patterns from fast spiking patterns in Monkeys G and C’s CO task in comparison with other thresholds ( data not shown ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides a key behavioral classification relevant to the study's analysis of neural activity in relation to movement speed.

fact: Movement onset time during the arm-reaching epoch was defined as the time when projected hand speed first exceeded 20% of its peak value during a reach.
source_span: To compute movement onset time for the arm-reaching epoch in the NR task , we used a method inspired by Churchland and Shenoy ( 2007 ) . First , the x and y cursor velocity over the course of the reach ( t x 2 ) was projected onto a unit vector pointing from the center to peripheral target . The norm of the projected cursor velocities yielded a single time series of projected speed ( t x 1 ) . The index and value of maximum projected hand speed was computed and called ( i , M ) . Starting at i , we scanned backwards in time ( i-1 , i-2 , … ) until the value of the projected hand speed fell below 20% of the peak hand speed ( 0 . 2*M , see Figure 1f ) . This timepoint was called the movement onset time and was used because it allowed for comparisons across different reach targets , animals , and experimental setups without having to define absolute hand velocity cutoffs .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes a key behavioral timing measure used to align neural data with movement, which is central to the study's analysis.

fact: Movement onset time was used as a standardized timepoint to compare reach behaviors across different targets, animals, and experimental setups without relying on absolute hand velocity cutoffs.
source_span: timepoint was called the movement onset time and was used because it allowed for comparisons across different reach targets , animals , and experimental setups without having to define absolute hand velocity cutoffs .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains a key methodological choice enabling consistent behavioral comparisons, relevant for understanding the study design.

fact: Cuzick’s test for trend was used to assess whether behavioral metrics showed significant ordered changes across groups defined by beta power levels.
source_span: Cuzick’s test for trend ( Cuzick , 1985 ) is a non-parametric test for significant ordering of groups in an increasing or decreasing manner ( two-tailed ) , and was used to assess significance of ordering of behavioral metrics according to the four beta target .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes a key statistical method used to link beta power groupings to behavioral outcomes, central to the study's main analyses.

fact: Trials were grouped into quartiles based on beta power estimates to test whether movement onset times varied systematically with beta power levels.
source_span: Trials were assigned group labels according to which quartile their power estimate for a particular frequency band falls in . For Figure 5a–c , non-normalized beta is computed in a window including the last 800 ms of the neurofeedback epoch . Trials were assigned labels depending on where they fell in the distribution of non-normalized beta power across trials: 0-25th percentile: label: 1 , 25th – 50th percentile: label: 2 , 50th – 75th percentile: label: 3 , and 75th – 100th percentile: label: 4 .
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes the key approach to categorize trials by beta power for behavioral correlation analyses.

selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies the subjects included in neural analyses, important for interpreting results.

fact: Spiking activity was compared between neurofeedback-induced beta oscillations and naturally occurring beta oscillations during reaching to assess differences in firing rates.
source_span: To assess whether units exhibited the same mean firing rate during neurofeedback-induced or naturally occurring beta oscillations , spiking activity was binned into 100 ms bins during NR trials and CO reaching trials . Spike counts during the slow , on-beta bins in the neurofeedback epoch of the NR task were compared with spike counts during slow , on-beta time points during the CO task .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes a principal comparison of neural activity across task contexts, central to the study's findings.

fact: A beta amplitude-to-spike rate mapping was estimated for individual units in both neurofeedback and natural reaching tasks to characterize how beta oscillations influence spiking activity.
source_span: To assess how individual units were influenced by ongoing beta oscillations in different task contexts , a beta amplitude-to-spike rate mapping was estimated for each unit in the two different tasks .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights a key analytical approach linking beta oscillations to neural firing, relevant to the study's main question.

fact: Beta amplitude was estimated using a bandpass filter from 25 to 40 Hz and the Hilbert transform applied to neural data during task trials.
source_span: Continuous beta amplitude was estimated for these time slices using a fifth order Butterworth bandpass filter from 25 to 40 Hz and then applying the Hilbert transform .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides a high-level description of how beta oscillations were quantified, important for understanding the neural analyses.

fact: The stability of the beta amplitude-to-spike rate relationship was assessed by comparing linear regression slopes derived from two non-overlapping data segments within the same task.
source_span: To assess the intra-task and inter-task stability of the beta amplitude to spike rate mapping , in Figure 6f and g , two equal , non-overlapping segments of data ... were used to estimate the beta amplitude to spike rate mapping . The slopes from the resultant linear regressions were plotted against one another .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes a key validation step for the neural data analysis, supporting the reliability of the findings.

fact: A logistic regression classifier was trained on spiking activity to distinguish pre-movement onset from post-movement onset periods in two different motor tasks.
source_span: To assess the information about movement onset contained in spiking activity during different parts of the NR and CO tasks , a logistic regression classifier was trained on spiking activity to discriminate pre-movement onset ( PreMO ) and post-movement onset ( PostMO ) .
selection_reasoning: This describes a key method used to analyze neural data related to movement onset, central to the study's main question.

selection_reasoning: This fact describes a key analytical approach to understand the relationship between beta oscillations and spike rates, relevant to the study's main findings.

fact: Using 75% of the data in each subset improved the stability of the beta amplitude-to-spike rate mapping correlations for Monkey C, which had limited CO task data.
source_span: Using 75% of data in each subset yielded more stable correlations and was used in Figure 6f–h and subsequent statistics .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights an important methodological adjustment to ensure reliable results, relevant to interpreting the findings.

selection_reasoning: This fact explains a key classification feature used in the analysis linking beta oscillations to movement-related neural activity.

fact: Optimal classification thresholds for movement onset prediction differed between monkeys, with 0.5 for Monkey G and 0.315 for Monkey C.
source_span: We found that optimal thresholds for maximizing percent correct classification wre 0 . 5 and 0 . 315 for Monkey G and Monkey C .
selection_reasoning: This fact indicates a key result about classifier performance and individual differences, relevant to interpreting the predictive neural signals.

source_span: Marburg virus , the Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus ( KSHV ) and Dengue virus all activate , and benefit from , expression of the transcription regulator nuclear erythroid 2-related factor 2 ( Nrf2 ) .

fact: This work reports the construction of robust proteochemometric (PCM) models based on 300,000 bioactivity data points measured against different HIV genotypes.

selection_reasoning: Describes the main methodological advance and dataset scale central to the study.

source_span: Given the nature of the PCM modeling procedure employed in this work , we were able to combine all resistance profiles of the three above drug classes in three single models , hence focusing on very large target space ( tens of thousands of different proteins ) in this work .

source_span: Another application of our models is the support of personalized drug regimen predictions . We have shown that our models are able to predict clinical resistance with a high degree of reliability .

fact: Sequences were encoded using Z-scales, which characterize physicochemical properties of amino acid side chains such as lipophilicity, size, and polarity.

The Z-scales are a previously published set of descriptors that characterize the physicochemical properties of the amino acids side chains . The resulting scales correlate to lipophilicity , size and polarity for each amino acid .
selection_reasoning: Describes a key methodological step enabling improved sequence representation in the models.

source_span: Models were constructed in the academic version of Pipeline Pilot 6 . 1 . 5 using the R-statistics package . Support vector machines ( SVM ) with a radial basis function kernel as coded in the e1071 package were used for model creation .

Optimal performance was reached at 97% , similarity defined as 1 minus the euclidean distance .
selection_reasoning: This explains how the model's reliability was assessed, which is important for understanding the model's validity.

fact: The PCM models showed robust performance with good validation parameters, with the protease inhibitor (PI) model performing best and the non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI) model performing worst.

The PI model shows the best performance , RMSE = 0 . 42 log units when trained on 5% of the full set and <0 . 30 log units when trained on 70% of the dataset . The NNRTI model the worst performance , RMSE = 0 . 70 log units when trained on 5% of the full set and <0 . 50 log units when trained on 70% of the dataset .

fact: Staphylococcus aureus is the leading cause of skin and soft tissue infections (SSTIs) in humans.
source_span: Staphylococcus aureus is the leading cause of skin and soft tissue infections ( SSTIs ) in humans [1 , 2] with S . aureus SSTIs resulting in over 11 million outpatient visits and almost 500 , 000 hospital admissions in the United States annually [3] .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides essential background on the clinical importance of S. aureus SSTIs, motivating the study.

fact: S. aureus SSTIs often form cutaneous abscesses that limit antibiotic penetration and efficacy.
source_span: S . aureus SSTIs routinely manifest as cutaneous abscesses which limit the penetration and efficacy of antibiotics [4] .
selection_reasoning: This explains a key clinical challenge in treating S. aureus SSTIs, justifying the need for alternative therapies.

fact: Community-acquired methicillin resistant S. aureus (CA-MRSA) skin infections are increasing in frequency in healthy individuals and are difficult to treat due to antibiotic resistance.
source_span: Community-acquired methicillin resistant S . aureus ( CA-MRSA ) skin infections are increasing in frequency in healthy individuals [5] and the treatment of these infections has become increasingly difficult due to the emergence of antibiotic resistance .
selection_reasoning: This highlights the growing public health problem and the need for new preventive strategies.

fact: An effective anti-S. aureus vaccine remains elusive, and a vaccine targeting specific clinical manifestations such as SSTIs may be needed.
source_span: The development of an anti-S . aureus vaccine offers a potential solution to prevent infection regardless of antibiotic resistance; however , although significant efforts have been made , an effective anti-S . aureus vaccine remains elusive . Given the wide spectrum of pathologies caused by this bacterium it is unlikely that a universal anti-S . aureus vaccine will ever be realised [6] , and instead , a vaccine targeting specific clinical manifestations may need to be pursued .
selection_reasoning: This frames the rationale for focusing on SSTI-specific vaccine targets.

fact: Staphylococcus aureus expresses up to 25 different cell wall-anchored (CWA) proteins that mediate adhesion, invasion, biofilm formation, and immune evasion.
source_span: S . aureus expresses up to 25 different cell wall-anchored ( CWA ) proteins , which are covalently linked to the peptidoglycan layer by the enzyme sortase A and are primarily involved in adhesion and invasion of host cells and tissues , biofilm formation and immune evasion [8] .
selection_reasoning: This provides biological background on the virulence factors relevant to infection.

fact: Sortase A-deficient mutants lacking most CWA proteins show reduced virulence and bacterial burden in skin abscess models.
source_span: Sortase A-deficient mutants , which lack the majority of cell surface bound CWA proteins , have reduced virulence in a murine kidney abscess model [9 , 10] , while in a skin abscess model , a sortase A-deficient mutant resulted in lower bacterial burden in the skin and a significantly reduced pathology compared to wild-type infected mice [11] .
selection_reasoning: This supports the importance of CWA proteins in SSTI pathogenesis.

fact: The role of individual CWA proteins during S. aureus SSTIs is poorly understood.
source_span: These studies indicate that CWA proteins are important during SSTIs and suggest that CWA proteins may be particularly important during the process of abscess formation . However , there is a paucity of information regarding the role of individual surface proteins during SSTIs .
selection_reasoning: This identifies the knowledge gap motivating the study.

fact: Clumping factor B (ClfB) is a cell wall-anchored protein that facilitates S. aureus nasal colonization by binding to the cornified envelope in the anterior nares.
source_span: The cell wall-anchored protein clumping factor B ( ClfB ) has previously been shown to facilitate S . aureus nasal colonization through high affinity interactions with the cornified envelope in the anterior nares .
selection_reasoning: This introduces ClfB and its known role, setting up the question about its role in SSTIs.

fact: The role of ClfB during skin and soft tissue infection (SSTI) has not been previously investigated.
source_span: However , the role of ClfB during skin and soft tissue infection ( SSTI ) has never been investigated .
selection_reasoning: This states the main research question addressed by the study.

fact: This study reveals a novel role for ClfB during S. aureus SSTIs, showing it is crucial in determining abscess structure and bacterial burden early in infection.
source_span: This study reveals a novel role for ClfB during SSTIs . ClfB is crucial in determining the abscess structure and bacterial burden early in infection and this is dependent upon a specific interaction with the ligand loricrin which is expressed within the abscess tissue .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding central to the study's contribution.

fact: ClfB interacts specifically with the ligand loricrin, which is expressed within abscess tissue during SSTIs.
source_span: ClfB is crucial in determining the abscess structure and bacterial burden early in infection and this is dependent upon a specific interaction with the ligand loricrin which is expressed within the abscess tissue .
selection_reasoning: This identifies the key molecular interaction underlying ClfB's role in SSTIs.

fact: Targeting ClfB with a model vaccine that induces both protective humoral and cellular responses leads to protection during S. aureus skin infection.
source_span: Targeting ClfB using a model vaccine that induced both protective humoral and cellular responses , leads to protection during S . aureus skin infection .
selection_reasoning: This demonstrates the translational significance of ClfB as a vaccine target.

fact: ClfB is identified as an important antigen for future vaccines specifically targeting S. aureus skin and soft tissue infections.
source_span: This study therefore identifies ClfB as an important antigen for future SSTI vaccines .
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the study's implication for vaccine development.

fact: Mice infected with a ClfB-deficient S. aureus strain formed significantly smaller abscess lesions and had reduced bacterial burden compared to mice infected with wild-type S. aureus.
source_span: Mice infected with LAC::lux ΔclfB formed significantly smaller abscess lesions on day 3–6 compared to mice infected with LAC::lux ( Fig 1A and 1B ) . The bioluminescence signal was also reduced in LAC::lux ΔclfB infected animals compared to LAC::lux infected mice ( Fig 1C and 1D ) . The reduction in bioluminescence signal was validated by quantifying the bacterial burden in the skin on day 3 ( Fig 1E ) and day 6 ( Fig 1F ) .
selection_reasoning: This experimental result provides direct evidence for ClfB's role in SSTI pathogenesis.

fact: ClfB affects both the rate of abscess formation and the overall size of the abscess formed during Staphylococcus aureus skin and soft tissue infections.
source_span: Taken together, these results demonstrate that ClfB affects both the rate of abscess formation and the overall size of the abscess formed, which ultimately leads to greater bacterial burden in the skin.
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding linking ClfB to abscess development and bacterial burden, central to the study's main question and significance.

fact: ClfB has an important function during Staphylococcus aureus skin and soft tissue infections, likely exerting its effect early in the infection process.
source_span: Crucially, these results have demonstrated for the first time that ClfB has an important function during S. aureus SSTIs, likely exerting its effect early in the infection process.
selection_reasoning: This highlights the novel discovery and timing of ClfB's role, important background and main conclusion.

fact: During nasal colonization, Staphylococcus aureus binding to the squamous epithelium is facilitated by the interaction between ClfB and the squamous cell envelope protein loricrin.
source_span: During nasal colonization, S. aureus binding to the squamous epithelium of the anterior nares is facilitated via the interaction between ClfB and the squamous cell envelope protein loricrin.
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the known ClfB-loricrin interaction, providing biological context for the study.

fact: Loricrin is present in the epidermal layer and in the abscess wall structure during Staphylococcus aureus subcutaneous abscess formation.
source_span: At 48 h post-infection loricrin is clearly visible in the epidermal layer of the skin, which is to be expected as it is a major component of the cornified envelope. Interestingly, it is also detected in the abscess wall structure following challenge with both LAC::lux and LAC::lux ΔclfB.
selection_reasoning: This fact supports the investigation of loricrin's role in abscess formation, linking to the main mechanism studied.

fact: Loricrin-deficient mice form significantly smaller abscesses and have reduced bacterial burden during Staphylococcus aureus skin and soft tissue infections compared to wild-type mice.
source_span: Lor-/- mice formed significantly smaller abscesses compared to WT mice and had reduced bioluminescence, indicating the presence of loricrin is important for abscess formation and bacterial burden during S. aureus SSTIs.
selection_reasoning: This finding demonstrates the importance of loricrin in infection severity, a key mechanistic and translational claim.

fact: Abscess formation is impaired in loricrin-deficient mice at 12 hours post infection, with less well-structured and smaller abscesses formed.
source_span: Importantly, it can be seen that abscess formation is impaired in Lor-/- mice at 12 hours post infection with overall less well-structured and smaller abscesses being formed.
selection_reasoning: This supports the timing and structural role of loricrin in abscess development, central to the study's mechanism.

fact: In wild-type mice, infection with Staphylococcus aureus lacking ClfB results in smaller abscess lesions and reduced bacterial burden compared to infection with wild-type bacteria.
source_span: WT mice that received LAC::lux ΔclfB formed smaller abscess lesions and had significantly reduced bioluminescence compared to WT mice that received LAC::lux which was confirmed by quantifying bacterial burden in the skin.
selection_reasoning: This fact directly links ClfB expression to virulence and abscess severity, a core experimental finding.

fact: In loricrin-deficient mice, there is no significant difference in abscess lesion size or bacterial burden between infection with Staphylococcus aureus lacking ClfB and wild-type bacteria.
source_span: There was no significant difference in abscess lesion area, bioluminescence or skin CFUs between Lor-/- mice that received LAC::lux or LAC::lux ΔclfB.
selection_reasoning: This shows that loricrin is required for ClfB-dependent virulence, a key mechanistic insight.

fact: Expression of loricrin within tissue during abscess formation facilitates the binding of Staphylococcus aureus via ClfB, contributing to the formation of a robust abscess.
source_span: Taken together these data suggest that expression of loricrin within the tissue during abscess formation facilitates the binding of S. aureus specifically via ClfB, thus contributing to the formation of a robust abscess.
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the main mechanism linking loricrin, ClfB, and abscess formation, central to the study's conclusions.

fact: Pre-incubation of Staphylococcus aureus with recombinant loricrin loop L2v reduces abscess lesion area and bacterial burden during skin infection in mice.
source_span: Mice that received LAC::lux+L2v had reduced abscess lesion area compared to the LAC::lux+GST group. In addition, bioluminescence signal was reduced throughout the infection period in LAC::lux+L2v infected mice compared to mice that received LAC::lux+GST and this reduction in bioluminescence was confirmed with a significant decrease in the bacterial burden in the skin on day 3 and 6 post-infection.
selection_reasoning: This demonstrates a potential therapeutic approach targeting the ClfB-loricrin interaction, important for translational relevance.

fact: Vaccination with ClfB combined with the TLR9 agonist CpG induces antigen-specific cellular and humoral immune responses in mice.
source_span: Immunization with ClfB in combination with CpG drove a significant increase in ClfB-specific IFNγ, IL-17 and IL-22 producing CD4+ T cells by inguinal lymph node cells compared to CpG-immunized mice. ClfB-specific CD8+ T cells producing IFNγ, IL-17 and IL-22 were also increased in the ILN of ClfB-vaccinated groups compared to the adjuvant alone group. Vaccination with ClfB also induced significantly elevated ClfB-specific serum IgG titres in mice compared to the control group.
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the key immunological outcome of the vaccine approach, central to the study's translational aim.

fact: Antibodies induced by ClfB vaccination inhibit the binding of ClfB-expressing bacteria to loricrin.
source_span: We confirmed that these antibodies were functional by investigating their ability to inhibit L. lactis expressing ClfB to bind to immobilised loricrin.
selection_reasoning: This supports the functional relevance of the vaccine-induced antibodies, important for vaccine efficacy claims.

fact: ClfB is a surface protein of Staphylococcus aureus that facilitates nasal colonization by binding to host ligands loricrin and cytokeratin 10.
source_span: Previous to this study , the main function attributed to ClfB was in facilitating S . aureus nasal colonization due to its ability to bind host ligands loricrin and cytokeratin 10 in the anterior nares [13–15].
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the known role of ClfB and sets the stage for investigating its role in skin infections.

fact: This study identifies ClfB as a virulence factor important for the pathogenesis of Staphylococcus aureus skin and soft tissue infections (SSTIs).
source_span: This study identifies , for the first time , an important role for ClfB in the pathogenesis of SSTIs and provides proof-of-concept that ClfB represents a good candidate antigen for inclusion in next-generation vaccines targeting S . aureus SSTI.

fact: Using a ClfB mutant strain of the clinically relevant CA-MRSA USA300 strain, the study demonstrates that ClfB contributes to virulence during S. aureus skin infection.
source_span: Using a clfB mutant in the clinically relevant CA-MRSA USA300 strain , LAC::lux , we demonstrate that ClfB is a virulence determinant during S . aureus skin infection.
selection_reasoning: This experimental evidence supports the key claim that ClfB is a virulence factor in skin infection.

fact: ClfB promotes abscess formation early during the infection process in skin infections caused by S. aureus.
source_span: Crucially , ClfB appears to exert its effect early during the infection process during initial formation of the abscess.
selection_reasoning: This clarifies the timing and mechanism of ClfB's role in pathogenesis.

fact: Loricrin, a host ligand for ClfB, is present not only in the outer skin layers but also within the wall of skin abscesses during S. aureus infection, likely due to disrupted expression during wound healing.
source_span: Immunohistochemistry analysis revealed that loricrin , an important ligand for ClfB , was present in the outermost layer of the skin , the corneal layer , as expected; however , loricrin also appeared to be present within the wall of the skin abscess structure of LAC::lux infected mice . Although loricrin is normally confined to the granular and corneal layers of the skin [22 , 23] , the expression and localisation of loricrin is disrupted during wound healing [24 , 25].
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the biological basis for ClfB-loricrin interaction in skin abscesses.

fact: Loricrin-deficient mice infected with S. aureus develop smaller abscesses with lower bacterial burden and reduced pathology compared to wild-type mice, indicating the importance of the ClfB-loricrin interaction in SSTIs.
source_span: Lor-/- mice infected s . c . with LAC::lux formed significantly smaller abscess , with lower bacterial burden and reduced pathology compared to WT infected mice , suggesting that the interaction between S . aureus and loricrin is crucial during SSTIs.
selection_reasoning: This genetic evidence supports the role of loricrin in mediating ClfB-dependent virulence.

fact: The reduction in abscess formation and infection severity in loricrin-deficient mice is specific to ClfB, as infection with a ClfB-deficient strain does not further reduce disease severity in these mice.
source_span: This effect appears to be ClfB-specific , and not due to ClfB binding to an alternative ligand in the skin , such as fibrinogen or keratin , as Lor-/- mice infected with LAC::lux ΔclfB did not display any further significant reduction in abscess formation or the overall severity of skin infection.

fact: Pre-incubation of S. aureus with recombinant loricrin blocks ClfB binding to native skin ligands and reduces bacterial burden and abscess size in infected mice.

selection_reasoning: This demonstrates a potential therapeutic approach targeting the ClfB-loricrin interaction.

fact: ClfB has been shown to mediate S. aureus adhesion to skin corneocytes in atopic dermatitis, suggesting its broader role in skin colonization and infection.
source_span: Interestingly , ClfB has also been shown to be a major player in mediating S . aureus adhesion to skin corneocytes in atopic dermatitis [26].
selection_reasoning: This fact provides additional context for the relevance of ClfB in skin-related diseases.

fact: Vaccination with ClfB combined with the CpG adjuvant induces antigen-specific cellular immune responses, including expansion of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells producing IFNγ, IL-17, and IL-22 in mice.
source_span: Immunization with ClfB+CpG induced significant expansion of antigen-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T cells capable of producing IFNγ , IL-17 and IL-22.
selection_reasoning: This describes the key immunological mechanism induced by the vaccine candidate.

fact: Vaccination with ClfB and CpG also induces significant levels of ClfB-specific neutralizing antibodies in mice.

fact: Mice vaccinated with ClfB and CpG develop significantly smaller abscess lesions and have reduced bacterial burden during S. aureus skin infection compared to control mice.

fact: Vaccination with ClfB combined with CpG adjuvant activates both humoral and cellular immune responses against Staphylococcus aureus.

This demonstrates that ClfB can activate both the humoral and cellular arms of the immune system which combined led to a substantial reduction in the severity of the subsequent LAC::lux skin infection
